device-level.title: v1 now includes `operate` actions. Which level does a paired device get, and how?
device-level.display: Chosen per device in the native pairing window

preview-size.title: You wrote 'the same as in the mac' for phone previews. Which parts carry over?
preview-size.display: Exactly as on the Mac: 50 MB, any path

tmux-stream.title: Your note: 'stream tmux so the user can control it from their phone, like Attach'. Is that in this change?
tmux-stream.display: In this change, full control at `configure` level

macos27-host.title: Where will K1 run on macOS 27? (a machine, a VM, a borrowed Mac)
macos27-host.value: why do we need a macos? I have my mac, it's just for signing right?

wildcard-detail.title: Wildcard bind with remote access: what the warning looks like
wildcard-detail.value: The gateway runs. GET /remote-access, `agetor remote status` and core.log show 'API is also reachable beyond loopback over plain HTTP'. Invariant 5 in the spec and security.md is amended to 'loopback, or a wildcard bind with that warning'.

auto-mode-guard.title: 'Yes, and use auto mode' from the phone counts as an operate action, with the unlock window
auto-mode-guard.value: Row 1 needs an `operate` device, a signature bound to the plan hash, and the unlock window (the same gate content gets on a task that runs without asking). Row 2 is respond and signed; row 3 is content.

plan-edit-scope.title: Mac side only for the plan-edit route
plan-edit-scope.value: This change adds its remote policy entry, content-level signing over the edited plan body, the router mapping, and coverage in the headless test client. The phone's plan editor belongs to the iOS app spec.
